reason: Conversation 2 correctly identified Er03 as the liquid/object-on-controls safety cut-off, gave the exact sensible first step (clear, clean and dry the panel, power cycle), stated no part is needed in most cases, and appropriately deferred to AEG service only if the code persists with a dry panel. Conversation 1 speculated about short-circuit or earth-leakage faults and 'permanent damage to the control PCB', imposed an unnecessary 24-hour lockout, bolted on an irrelevant tripping-electrics safety panel, and then gave only a one-line reply when the customer reported it was already fixed, never explaining what Er03 actually means.
